 61 Applicants for Every Home: MHADA Pune Lottery Draws Record 2.74 Lakh Entries 
 News 
 Pune 
 November 11, 2026 by Divyani Sharma 
 Pune: The Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority’s (MHADA) Pune Board has received a record 2,74,068 applications with earnest money deposits for its lottery of 4,462 homes. That works out to about 61 applicants for every home, the highest response the Pune Board has seen for a housing lottery. The draw will be held on December 1.
 The registration and application process ended on October 30. In all, 3,25,077 applications were submitted, but only those who paid the mandatory earnest money deposit, 2,74,068 of them, are eligible for the lottery. Officials said the turnout was far above what they had expected. In earlier Pune Board lotteries, the highest number of applications with deposits was around 2.25 lakh. This time it has gone up to nearly 2.75 lakh. The homes fall under the economically weaker section (EWS) and low-income group (LIG) categories. MHADA fixed the earnest money at ₹15,000 for EWS homes and ₹20,000 for LIG homes. Every applicant also paid an application fee of ₹708. Officials said the Pune Board has collected about ₹567.54 crore from deposits and fees together. Applications will now be scrutinised, after which the final list of eligible applicants will be published. Officials said only a small number of applications are usually rejected at this stage, so nearly 2.74 lakh applicants are expected to take part in the draw. 
Make Pune Mirror My Trusted Source 
 Registration for homes under the 15% integrated housing scheme and the 20% comprehensive housing scheme began on August 24. The board had to extend the deadline three times because of technical problems during the application process. The MahaIT system was unavailable between October 16 and 20 for technical reasons, which stopped the verification of applicants’ documents. The board gave a third extension so the pre-lottery work could be completed. Once the window closed, the Pune Board finished the pending document verification and announced the final application figures. Applicants who do not win a home will get their earnest money back after the December 1 draw. The ₹708 application fee is non-refundable.
